title: Voice leading and guide tones
description: Hold common tones, move by step, and trace 3 and 7 through ii–V–I.

cards.back: How the individual notes of one chord move into the next. Good voice leading keeps most notes common or close, even when roots jump.

cards.front: What are guide tones, and why do they matter more than roots?
cards.back: The third and seventh of each chord. They carry quality and function, so tracing them shows the harmony more clearly than tracing roots.

cards.front: Between two chords, apply which three steps in order?
cards.back: 1. Hold common tones on the same string and fret. 2. Move remaining voices by the smallest step (half or whole). 3. Resolve tensions: leading tones usually rise, sevenths usually fall.

cards.front: In C major, give 3 and 7 of Dm7, G7, and Cmaj7.
cards.back: Dm7: F and C. G7: B and F. Cmaj7: E and B.

cards.front: Trace the two guide-tone lines of a major ii V I in C.
cards.back: C B B (7 of Dm7 falls a half step to 3 of G7, then stays as 7 of Cmaj7). F F E (3 of Dm7 stays as 7 of G7, then falls a half step to 3 of Cmaj7).

cards.front: Does that ii V I guide-tone pattern hold in other keys?
cards.back: Yes, for a major ii V I with seventh chords: 7→3 down a half step, 3→7 common, then 7→3 down a half step.

cards.front: Trace guide tones of Dm7b5 – G7 – Cm7 in C minor.
cards.back: Thirds F, B, Eb. Sevenths C, F, Bb. Lines: C B Bb and F F Eb. First line moves by half step twice.

cards.front: From A7 to D7, what happens to both guide tones?
cards.back: Both fall by half step: G (7 of A7) to F# (3 of D7), and C# (3 of A7) to C (7 of D7).

cards.front: Does minimal motion apply to the bass the same way?
cards.back: No. Upper voices stay close; the bass usually carries roots and may jump. Voice leading and bass note are separate choices.

cards.front: Give the ii V I shells in C (frets and the top two notes).
cards.back: Dm7 x5x56x (D, C, F). G7 3xx46x (G, B, F). Cmaj7 x3x45x (C, B, E). Strings 3 and 2: 5/6, 4/6, 4/5.

cards.front: Across that C ii V I, how far do the upper two fingers move?
cards.back: Only C to B (one fret) and F to E (one fret). The bass is free to jump because roots move in fifths.

cards.front: Move those C shells up two frets for D major.
Trace guide tones of Em7 A7 Dmaj7 (ii V I in D).
cards.back: Thirds G C# F#. Sevenths D G C#. Lines: D C# C# and G G F#.

cards.front: Trace guide tones of Am7 D7 Gmaj7 (in G).
cards.back: Thirds C F# B. Sevenths G C F#. Lines: G F# F# and C C B.

cards.front: A7 shell 5x56xx to D7 shell x5x57x. Name each guide-tone move.
cards.back: G falls to F#, and C# falls to C. Track pitch classes, not frets — they sit on different strings.

cards.front: For Cmaj7 Am7 Dm7 G7, list notes shared by each neighboring pair.
cards.back: Cmaj7 to Am7 share C E G. Am7 to Dm7 share A C. Dm7 to G7 share F, and C falls to B.
